---
title: "Figure 2.3: LAC: International Bond Issuance"
---

![Python: `python/fig-2-3.py`](../images/python/fig-2-3.png)

Annual bond issuance by country as stacked bars. Red dots mark issuance in
January–September of each earlier year, for comparison with the latest,
partial year.

**New in this chart:**

- a stack of nine series;
- dots on the bars;
- a label with a pointer line;
- a two-column legend in Excel's row-by-row order.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 5 rows (2022 to 2026):

| category | Rest of LAC | CAPDR/CARIB | Uruguay | ... | Brazil | Jan-Sep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 1.15 | 10.72 | 0.99 | ... | 10.73 | 44.92 |

## The script

### The stack

```python
categories = data["category"].astype(str)

# Stacking order, from the bottom up, and colours.
stack_colours = {
    "Rest of LAC": "#000000",
    "CAPDR/CARIB": "#4F8A10",
    ...
    "Brazil": "#08679B",
}
```

The years are converted to text, because they are used as labels under
category positions. The dictionary order is the stacking order from the
bottom up, and is read off the published chart.

```python
x = np.arange(len(data))
bottom = np.zeros(len(data))
bars = {}
for series, colour in stack_colours.items():
    bars[series] = ax.bar(x, data[series], bottom=bottom, width=0.56, color=colour)
    bottom += data[series].to_numpy()
```

This is the standard [stacked bars](../techniques.qmd#sec-stacked) loop, with
one addition. What `ax.bar()` returns, the drawn bars, is kept in the
dictionary `bars`, so the legend can be built later in a different order.

### The dots and the pointer

```python
# Red dots: issuance in January-September of each earlier year, for
# comparison with the last bar. There is no dot on the last bar itself.
jan_sep = data["Jan-Sep"].iloc[:-1]
ax.scatter(x[:-1], jan_sep, s=90, color="red", edgecolor="black",
           linewidth=1.2, zorder=3)
```

`.iloc[:-1]` selects all rows except the last, and `x[:-1]` does the same
for the positions. In Python, `-1` counts from the end.

`scatter` draws the dots, with `s` the dot area in points squared.
`zorder=3` puts them on top of the bars.

```python
ax.annotate("Jan-Sep", xy=(x[0], jan_sep.iloc[0] + 3.5), xytext=(x[0] - 0.1, 83),
            color="red", fontsize=9, ha="left", va="bottom",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="#A6A6A6", linewidth=1.2,
                            shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))
```

The "Jan-Sep" label sits above the first bar at height 83, with a grey line
down to just above the first dot. `xy` is the point the line goes to and
`xytext` is where the text is. `shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0` stop matplotlib from
shortening the line at either end. See [Text, arrows and
coordinates](../techniques.qmd#sec-text).

### The legend in Excel's order

```python
# Legend in two columns, read row by row: Brazil, Chile / Colombia, Mexico ...
# (matplotlib fills legend columns top to bottom, so reorder accordingly).
row_order = list(stack_colours)[::-1]
legend_order = row_order[0::2] + row_order[1::2]
ax.legend([bars[s] for s in legend_order], legend_order,
          loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.03, 1.02), ncol=2,
          handlelength=1.0, handleheight=1.0, labelspacing=0.15,
          columnspacing=1.8, fontsize=9)
```

The legend lists the countries from the top of the stack down (Brazil,
Chile, Colombia, ...). It has two columns, read across: Brazil and Chile on
the first row.

1. **Top of the stack first.** `[::-1]` reverses the list.
2. **Two columns.** matplotlib fills the first column completely before
   starting the second. The list is therefore reordered: every other entry
   starting from the first (`[0::2]`) fills the left column, and the rest
   (`[1::2]`) the right column.

See [Legends](../techniques.qmd#sec-legends).

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-2-3.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-2-3.py"}
"""Figure 2.3: LAC: International Bond Issuance."""
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart

STEM = "fig-2-3"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)
categories = data["category"].astype(str)

# Stacking order, from the bottom up, and colours.
stack_colours = {
    "Rest of LAC": "#000000",
    "CAPDR/CARIB": "#4F8A10",
    "Uruguay": "#9B6AB0",
    "Peru": "#FDBF22",
    "Paraguay": "#8EC7E0",
    "Mexico": "#666666",
    "Colombia": "#D2691E",
    "Chile": "#009999",
    "Brazil": "#08679B",
}

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="LAC: International Bond Issuance",
    subtitle="(Billions of US dollars)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: Bond Radar; and IMF staff calculations.\n"
        "Note: Includes sovereign and corporate/financial bond issuances. CAPDR\n"
        "= Central America, Panama, and the Dominican Republic; CARIB =\n"
        "Caribbean; LAC = Latin America and the Caribbean."
    ),
    caption_size=8.4,
    left=0.35,
    right=0.15,
    bottom_gap=0.3,
)

x = np.arange(len(data))
bottom = np.zeros(len(data))
bars = {}
for series, colour in stack_colours.items():
    bars[series] = ax.bar(x, data[series], bottom=bottom, width=0.56, color=colour)
    bottom += data[series].to_numpy()

# Red dots: issuance in January-September of each earlier year, for
# comparison with the last bar. There is no dot on the last bar itself.
jan_sep = data["Jan-Sep"].iloc[:-1]
ax.scatter(x[:-1], jan_sep, s=90, color="red", edgecolor="black",
           linewidth=1.2, zorder=3)
ax.annotate("Jan-Sep", xy=(x[0], jan_sep.iloc[0] + 3.5), xytext=(x[0] - 0.1, 83),
            color="red", fontsize=9, ha="left", va="bottom",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="#A6A6A6", linewidth=1.2,
                            shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))

ax.set_xticks(x, categories)
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(data) - 0.5)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=3, pad=5)

ax.set_ylim(0, 180)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(30))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=3)

# Legend in two columns, read row by row: Brazil, Chile / Colombia, Mexico ...
# (matplotlib fills legend columns top to bottom, so reorder accordingly).
row_order = list(stack_colours)[::-1]
legend_order = row_order[0::2] + row_order[1::2]
ax.legend([bars[s] for s in legend_order], legend_order,
          loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.03, 1.02), ncol=2,
          handlelength=1.0, handleheight=1.0, labelspacing=0.15,
          columnspacing=1.8, fontsize=9)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
